repl.title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning for the Ly$α$ Forest: CNN-Based Absorber Detection and Characterization
repl.summary: The Ly$\alpha$ forest is a powerful probe of the intergalactic medium and small-scale matter distribution, but deriving absorber properties traditionally requires computationally expensive Voigt-profile fitting. We present a convolutional neural network (CNN) that identifies and characterizes H I Ly$\alpha$ absorbers directly from quasar spectra. The model is trained on synthetic spectra generated from the IllustrisTNG simulation and fitted with the VIPER Voigt-profile fitting code to provide training labels. The network simultaneously predicts absorber presence, column density ($N_{\rm HI}$), Doppler parameter ($b_{\rm HI}$), and line centroid. On simulated spectra, the CNN reproduces the viper reference catalogue with an F1 score of $\sim$0.8, with mean absolute errors of $\sim$0.18 in $\log N_{\rm HI}$ and $\sim$0.10 in $\log b_{\rm HI}$. It reproduces the H I column density distribution function and the $b_{\rm HI}$--$N_{\rm HI}$ relation obtained from viper, recovering similar CDDF slopes and a lower-envelope relation with an RMS difference of only 0.36 km s$^{-1}$. Applied to UVES spectra, performance decreases to an F1 score of $\sim$0.5, with mean absolute errors of $\sim$0.35 in $\log N_{\rm HI}$ and $\sim$0.22 in $\log b_{\rm HI}$. Latent-space analysis reveals a significant domain shift between the simulated and UVES spectra, contributing to the reduced performance. Nevertheless, the CNN reproduces the observed CDDF and $b_{\rm HI}$--$N_{\rm HI}$ distributions obtained from the viper catalogue, yielding CDDF slopes consistent with VIPER and a lower-envelope RMS difference of 3.20 km s$^{-1}$ relative to viper. Monte Carlo dropout is implemented during inference to quantify predictive uncertainties. Together with its computational efficiency, the method provides a scalable and uncertainty-aware framework for Ly$\alpha$ forest analysis in upcoming spectroscopic surveys.

repl.title: Anisotropic separate universe : Long-wavelength perturbations and conserved quantities
repl.summary: We study the superhorizon evolution of linear perturbations in an anisotropic Bianchi type I universe with a scalar field coupled to a U(1) gauge field. The analysis employs the spatial gradient expansion in the uniform-$\mathcal{N}$ gauge, in which the local number of $e$-folds is unperturbed. In this gauge, the complete set of leading-order long-wavelength solutions, including both even- and odd-parity perturbations, can be constructed from variations of homogeneous Bianchi type I solutions, subject to the momentum and Gauss constraints. The conserved Wronskian found in isotropic multi-field inflation is generalized to the anisotropic system. Together with the shear and electric-flux integration constants, it allows the curvature perturbation on uniform-$\mathcal{N}$ hypersurfaces to be expressed in terms of background variations and time integrals. The conserved comoving curvature perturbations are then obtained by adding this intrinsic curvature contribution to the familiar $\delta N$ contribution arising from the change of time slicing. We also derive a relation between the curvature perturbation and a metric perturbation that reduces to the plus-polarized tensor mode in the isotropic limit, and discuss a nonlinear extension of the formalism.

repl.title: Mean-field interpretation of star-in-a-box simulations of red giants
repl.summary: Context: The origin of magnetic fields and the dynamo mechanism in red giants are still not fully understood. Aims: We aim to interpret the dynamo behaviour of global 3D simulations of red giants using mean-field dynamo models. Methods: We use mean-field models constrained by the differential rotation profile extracted from 3D simulations. We perform $\alpha^2$, $\alpha\Omega$, and $\alpha^2\Omega$ mean-field dynamo simulations, varying the strength of the $\alpha$ effect and the differential rotation. Results: The mean-field models can reproduce the growth rate of several 3D runs. The morphology of the large-scale magnetic field is better reproduced for the slowly rotating 3D cases than for the rapidly rotating ones. Faster rotation enhances dynamo action and it also modifies the dominant mode of the dynamo. Rapidly rotating 3D runs produce predominantly non-axisymmetric equatorial dipoles instead of axisymmetric fields at slower rotation. Mean-field models are supercritical even in the absence of differential rotation, indicating $\alpha^2$ dynamo action. By contrast, models using the $\alpha\Omega$ approximation require sufficiently strong differential rotation to become supercritical. Conclusions: Our results suggest that the magnetic field in red giants requires dynamo action. In our mean-field runs, differential rotation speeds up the magnetic decay, disfavouring the idea of a persistent fossil magnetic field in red giants as the explanation for the observed surface fields.

repl.title: Beyond Spin: QCD Magnetars
repl.summary: We present a unified framework in which anomalous X-ray pulsars (AXPs), soft gamma-ray repeaters (SGRs), superluminous supernovae (SLSNe-I), luminous fast blue optical transients (LFBOTs), and fast radio bursts (FRBs) originate from quark deconfinement in the core of a massive neutron star (NS). Spontaneous ferromagnetism in the deconfined phase generates ~10^18 G core fields, producing a highly magnetized hybrid star (HS) -- the ``QCD magnetar'' -- whose surface field is set by NS mass, not birth spin. The Quark-Nova (QN) that forms the HS ejects ~ 0.01M_sun of neutron-rich outer layers, powering a kilonova and leaving the HS crustless for centuries. During this phase, magnetic instabilities at the hadron--quark interface release rising flux ropes that power X-ray-quiet FRBs; as the crust reforms, the source evolves into an X-ray-loud AXP&SGR. Two parameters govern the model: a critical mass M_dec triggering deconfinement, and a critical period P_fast separating fast and slow rotators. Fast rotators inject spin-down energy into the QN ejecta, producing an LFBOT -- directly observable once the SN ejecta is optically thin, or via binary accretion with no preceding SN; otherwise the LFBOT is reprocessed by the SN ejecta into an SLSN-I. A Bayesian Monte Carlo population synthesis reproduces the observed rates of AXPs\&SGRs, SLSNe-I, and LFBOTs with M_dec ~ 2.1M_sun and P_fast ~ 5.5 ms, and predicts non-merger r-process signatures and kilonovae from isolated NSs, with or without an LFBOT. The QN ejecta also carries its own DM and RM, independent of environment, predicted to appear as excess dispersion and rotation measure in FRBs in addition to the Galactic, host, and intergalactic contributions. These provide direct observational tests of the hadron--quark phase transition and ferromagnetic ordering in dense quark matter.

repl.title: Comparison of the Neutron Star Birth Function from Core-Collapse Supernova Simulations with Observations
repl.summary: Using the mapping between progenitor core structure and the gravitational mass of neutron stars derived from sophisticated 3D supernova simulations, we construct the theoretical mass distribution of neutron stars at birth and investigate how it might comport with neutron star mass function measurements. In the process, we explore the effects of islands of black hole formation and subsequent mass accretion. We show that supernova theory can explain the observed neutron star mass function from its lower-mass peak near $\sim$1.35 $M_{\odot}$ to its higher-mass tail. Moreover, we suggest, but do not prove, that the lower predicted kick speeds expected during the birth of lower-mass neutron stars and the higher expected kick speeds expected on average for higher mass neutron stars may together sculpt the observed mass function in desired directions. The upshot of all these influences is to imprint upon the measured neutron star mass function features that reflect the varied physics of both neutron star origins and the neutron-star/black-hole dichotomy. Very approximately, we derive a black hole birth fraction of $\sim$19.6\%. In summary, we suggest that supernova theory can now be used to explain, however provisionally, various measured attributes of the population of compact objects and that an era of productive engagement between supernova theory and observation is at hand.

repl.title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: Passband Measurements with an Analysis of Systematic Errors
repl.summary: We present measurements of the spectral response of the four Advanced ACTPol (AdvACT) multichroic detector arrays, which observed in frequency bands centered near 30, 40, 90, 150, and 220 GHz. The passbands were measured with a Fourier transform spectrometer (FTS) combined with coupling optics that direct and match the output of the FTS to the AdvACT receiver. We perform optical simulations of the FTS and coupling optics in order to model frequency-dependent systematic effects in this system, examining the systematics of each individual measurement component in detail. We use these simulations to apply corrections to the measurements and evaluate the remaining systematic uncertainty. We combine these systematic estimates with statistical errors to determine the measured passbands and their uncertainties from our FTS measurement, which are typically $0.75$ to $1.5\%$ per detector array for the central frequency. We present the passband characteristics for all measurements made by ACT in a common framework. Additionally, we discuss in detail limits set by the systematics in our measurements as well as ways to minimize the systematics of each component to improve passband measurements in the future.

repl.title: AI-Assisted Extraction of Follow-up Observations from GCN Circulars in Astro-COLIBRI
repl.summary: We present a new Astro-COLIBRI component that converts free-text GCN Circulars into structured, event-linked follow-up records and combines them with reports submitted directly by the community. A continuously running listener associates new Circulars with transient events, applies deterministic pre-analysis, and invokes a schema-constrained large language model to extract photometry, contacts, redshifts, and related metadata. The records are normalized into a common event-level database and exposed through the web and mobile interfaces as report summaries, contact tools, optical-afterglow context figures, and downloadable CSV or VOTable products. All 1,775 Circulars of an operational evaluation corpus covering the first half of 2026 completed the workflow without failures. An internal human audit of 210 Circulars found 223 of 231 assessed reports (96.5%) fully confirmed, each of the eight remaining ones containing at least one incorrect field, predominantly associated with observation timing and facility attribution. Extracted redshifts agree with three published compilations for 91.7 to 99.3% of the events they share, every disagreement tracing to a limit, a candidate-host estimate, or a later-refined value rather than to a misread Circular. The extraction also recovers 90 to 97% of the redshifts those compilations list for bursts it processed. Applied to the GCN archive since 2016, the pipeline yields 68,393 observations from 26,811 reports across 5,787 transient events, and now runs in real time on new Circulars. The reusable parsing and normalization pipeline is released as the open-source Python package astro-colibri-circular-parser.

repl.title: The Road to Normalcy: Environment-Driven Evolutionary Pathways for Primordial Black Holes
repl.summary: We investigate how cosmological environment regulates the evolution of primordial black hole (PBH) seeds in the early universe using a suite of hydrodynamical simulations. PBHs, formed during the radiation dominated epoch, offer a possible source of early BH seeds that does not require prior star formation. We find that PBHs follow distinct evolutionary pathways depending on the gas supply and halo assembly history. In underdense regions, limited inflow suppresses both accretion and star formation, producing faint, metal-poor systems, while in overdense environments, sustained gas inflow drives rapid BH growth and the formation of compact, centrally concentrated stellar components. These differences lead to large variations in BH-to-stellar mass ratio, metallicity, and morphology, collectively bracketing a range of possible evolutionary pathways for PBH-seeded systems. Some pathways pass through a phase with compact stellar structure and elevated BH-to-stellar mass ratio that resembles observed Little Red Dots, before evolving into more extended galaxy--AGN systems. Our results suggest that both the initial seed properties and cosmological environment jointly shape early BH--galaxy co-evolution, while subsequent environmental regulation can erase the memory of the initial seeding channel.

repl.title: Revisiting the enigmatic sixth star cluster in the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy
repl.summary: The Fornax dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxy is one of only two Local Group dSphs that host a population of globular star clusters (GCs), the present-day properties of which have often been used to investigate the nature of the dark matter. An additional overdensity of stars called Fornax 6, lying at a projected distance of $\sim$0.3 kpc from the galaxy centre, was recently identified as a sixth GC residing in Fornax. However, this conclusion was based on relatively shallow photometric observations and a limited number of spectra. Here, we reinvestigate the nature of Fornax 6 by analysing MUSE/Wide-Field-Mode observations alongside deep GMOS-S imagery. Using a sample of 131 spectra of red giant and red clump stars, we confirm the Fornax 6 overdensity as a distinct chemo-dynamical component with respect to the surrounding field population. Specifically, we identify 43 likely members associated with the cluster, from which we measure $\rm [Fe/H]=-0.63\pm0.03\,$dex, $\overline{v_{los}} = 50.8^{+0.8}_{-0.7}\, \rm km\,s^{-1}$, and $\sigma_v = 3.3^{+1.4}_{-1.9}\, \rm km\,s^{-1}$. The main-sequence turn-off, observed here for the first time, strongly suggests that these stars are coeval and well described by a $\sim$3 Gyr old isochrone. The cluster is characterised by an irregular morphology, a large half-light radius ($R_h=8.8^{+1.1}_{-1.3}\,$pc), a small flattening ($e<0.26$, 68\% upper limit), and low luminosity ($M_V = -5.0 \pm 0.4$). Our improved characterisation of Fornax 6 supports its classification as a genuine low-mass cluster likely undergoing tidal disruption, making it the youngest and most metal-rich member of Fornax's unique GC system.

repl.title: JWST/NIRSpec Reveals Diverse Nuclear Environments in Dwarf Galaxies Hosting AGN
repl.summary: Dwarf galaxies, in the $\Lambda$CDM framework, are expected to dominate the galaxy number density at all redshifts. As such, studying AGN in these systems, including characterizing their local environments and emission properties, is essential in obtaining a comprehensive view of the AGN population and their influence on their host galaxy. To this end, we present JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of four dwarf galaxies (M$_\star<$10$^{9.5}\;$M$_\odot$) with evidence of AGN activity. Utilizing the improvements in resolution and sensitivity offered by JWST, we investigate the emission features of the central kiloparsec of these dwarfs. Our findings include the detection of over 100 emission lines across our sample, including coronal lines with ionization potentials greater than 300 eV. The nuclear spectra show diverse emission features. In two galaxies, we measure strong contributions from hot dust to the infrared continuum. We also detect both PAH and coronal line emission within 100 parsecs of the nuclei in three galaxies. We estimate the hot H$_2$ gas mass to be between 1--20 M$_\odot$ within 300 pc across our sample, where both thermal and non-thermal excitation are involved. Lastly, spatial flux maps reveal varied emission structures across all observed gas phases, ranging from radial symmetry around the nucleus to elongated plumes. Kinematic maps also show each galaxy has unique velocity structures despite all being isolated, affirming the diversity of rotation curves problem, a long standing tension between simulations and observations. These results showcase the unique and varied nuclear environments that can be found in dwarf galaxies hosting AGN.

repl.title: Beyond Pebble Isolation: Diverse Pathways to Giant Planet Formation Across Stellar and Orbital Scales
repl.summary: Context. Giant planet formation requires reaching crossover mass, i.e., when the mass of the gaseous envelope becomes equal to the mass of the core, within the disc's lifetime. The formation process depends critically on the orbital distance and stellar mass. Aims. We simulate planet formation via pebble accretion up to crossover mass around stellar hosts with masses of 0.1-1.5 M_Sun considering a range of formation locations, with and without Type I migration. Methods. We use a modified version of MESA that couples pebble accretion, gas accretion, and disc evolution. Results. We find that cold/warm Jupiters form, whereas in-situ formation fails at short orbital separations: viscous heating raises the isolation mass enough to assemble adequate cores, but the accompanying high disc temperature prevents cooling and suppresses gas giant formation. This supports migration-based explanations for the origin of hot Jupiters. At large orbital distances, crossover can be reached before pebble isolation mass. This is possible due to efficient envelope contraction in the cold, low-opacity outer disc. Inferred core masses at crossover range between about 1 and 20 M_Earth. Conclusions. Pebble accretion accommodates multiple formation pathways. Giant planets can also have very small cores. Overall, different formation conditions significantly influence planetary growth and can explain the diversity in compositions and internal structures observed in the exoplanet population.

repl.title: Initial clustering of primordial black holes: A general formulation for arbitrary local non-Gaussianity
repl.summary: Initial spatial clustering of primordial black holes (PBHs) induced by local-type non-Gaussianity (LNG) can substantially modify cosmological constraints on PBH abundance. Several inflationary scenarios that enhance curvature perturbations at small scales relevant to PBH formation predict LNG that is not necessarily perturbative. Therefore, it is crucial to establish a theoretical framework capable of investigating the initial clustering induced by arbitrary LNG. Here, we present a general analytical formulation for the PBH two-point correlation function applicable to arbitrary LNGs in the alternative approach. Under the assumptions that PBHs form only at the large peaks of perturbations, and that large-scale modes weakly modulate the local variance of small-scale perturbations, we derive an analytic expression for the PBH bias parameter, directly connecting initial clustering to the primordial trispectrum in the collapsed limit. We demonstrate the versatility of our formula by computing the bias parameters in the ultra-slow-roll inflation, curvaton, and modulated reheating scenarios. We also formally generalize the framework to broad power spectra to account for correlations across different PBH mass scales. Because our formulation does not rely on weak or perturbative non-Gaussianity assumptions, our result provides a universal theoretical basis for evaluating initial clustering impact on PBH observables.

repl.title: Late-Time Evolution of the Massive Stellar Merger M101 OT2015-1
repl.summary: Luminous red novae (LRNe) are astronomical transients arising from unstable mass transfer and common envelope phases in close binary systems, eventually culminating in stellar mergers. Their cold, expanding ejecta provide the ideal conditions for molecule and dust formation. We investigate the late-time dust and molecular evolution of the LRN M101 OT2015-1, a high-mass LRN progenitor ($18\pm 1$M$_\odot$), using multi-band near-infrared (NIR) and mid-infrared (MIR) observations spanning up to ~5 years post-outburst. Archival and unpublished photometry from NEOWISE, Spitzer, Keck NIRC2 and MOSFIRE, are interpolated via 2D Gaussian process regression. Spectral energy distributions (SEDs) are modelled with 1D spherical radiative transfer models to track the evolution of dust mass, dust temperature, and central source properties. At +150d post-peak, the SED is well-fit by a pure stellar blackbody ($T_{\rm eff}=3330$K) with negligible dust (log$M_{\rm dust}/$M$_\odot<-6.36$). Rapid dust condensation begins around day +200 ($T_{\rm dust}=1591$K), with dust mass increasing to log$M_{\rm dust}/$M$_\odot =-3.65$ and optical depth reaching $\tau_V =64$ by +1300d. A prominent NIR re-brightening at ~600d ($M_K=-12.04$), accompanied by a dust reheating bump ($T_{\rm dust}=1567$K), highlights a second phase of dust nucleation likely driven by shock interactions. Low-resolution NIR MOSFIRE spectra are analysed for line identification and also using an LTE isothermal slab model to characterise CO molecular features. The MOSFIRE spectra reveal an O-rich environment with photospheric expansion velocities of ~$520-620$km s$^{-1}$, as measured in the Pa$\beta$ emission line, and high CO column densities (log$N_{\rm CO}$/cm$^{-2}=20.9$ and $20.7$ at +142d and +197d, respectively). These results confirm that LRNe are prolific producers of cosmic dust and are efficient molecular factories.

repl.title: Tidal Dissipation from Circularization in Kepler Binaries
repl.summary: Understanding tidal dissipation is a requisite step for explaining the evolution of systems such as short-period binaries. This understanding has not yet been achieved, and in fact there are many different approaches to modelling tides. By using Bayesian analysis on a system-by-system basis, we provide additional constraints on dissipation for 105 short-period Sun-like Kepler binaries. We account for period-dependent $Q$ and stellar evolution, and propagate observational uncertainties to uncertainties in our constraints. We find a group constraint of $\log Q_*' \approx 6.75$, with no apparent dependence on tidal period. We also do not detect mass dependence for $Q$. Our inferred prescription for the tidal dissipation successfully reproduces the unexpected overlap between almost perfectly circular and significantly non-circular orbits in binaries of Sun-like stars reported by J. J. Zanazzi.

repl.title: Molecular mapping of an exoplanet with JWST: detection of NH$_3$ and HCN in the temperate super-Jupiter Epsilon Indi Ab
repl.summary: Epsilon Indi Ab is currently the coldest, and one of the closest, directly imaged exoplanets (T$_{\rm eff}$ = 275 K, d = 3.6 pc). It offers a unique opportunity to test our understanding of the physical and chemical properties of gas giants across the full temperature range spanned by hotter directly imaged exoplanets and the cooler giants of the Solar System. We characterize the atmosphere of Epsilon Indi Ab using infrared spectroscopic observations. We present JWST spectroscopic observations of Epsilon Indi Ab obtained with MIRI in the medium-resolution spectrograph mode (4.9-27.9 $\mu$m) and NIRSpec in the integral field unit mode (2.87-5.27 $\mu$m). The data are highly contaminated by the stellar light from the bright host star. We therefore adopt a high-pass filtering and cross-correlation approach based on petitRADTRANS atmospheric models to detect the planetary signal and specific molecules. The cross-correlation analysis enables a robust detection of the planet with both instruments (up to S/N = 15.0). Using molecular mapping, we securely identify the presence of NH$_3$ (maximum S/N = 14.4), H$_2$O (maximum S/N = 11.3), HCN (S/N = 5.3) and marginally detect PH$_3$ (S/N = 4.1), CH$_4$ (S/N = 3.8), C$_2$H$_2$ (S/N = 3.9) and CO$_2$ (S/N = 2.6). In particular, Epsilon Indi Ab becomes the coldest exoplanet in which NH$_3$ and HCN have been identified so far. The presence of HCN likely implies intense vertical mixing. These first results confirm that infrared spectroscopy combined with cross-correlation techniques can be used to characterize the atmosphere of directly imaged exoplanets with JWST, even when the contamination by the host star is critical.

repl.title: Wave-Optics Imprints of Warm Dark Matter Subhalos with Prompt Cusps on Strongly Lensed Gravitational Waves
repl.summary: Dark matter halos are expected to form with a prompt $\rho \propto r^{-3/2}$ density cusp at their centres, and in warm dark matter (WDM) cosmologies these cusps can dominate the inner structure of the low-mass subhalos that survive free-streaming suppression. We investigate whether that inner structure is visible to gravitational waves lensed in the wave-optics (WO) regime. Extending the strong lensing WO diffraction-integral framework to WDM, we generate subhalo populations with the {\sc sashimi-w} semi-analytic model, assign each subhalo a prompt cusp through a cusp-halo relation, and compute the frequency-dependent amplification factor $F(f)$ across the LISA band over 500 independent realisations for $m_\chi \in \{6, 10, 20, 40, 80, 100\}$~keV. The signal is governed by the overlap between the WDM-suppressed subhalo mass function and the $m_{\rm sub} \sim 10^{4}$ to $10^{7}\,M_\odot$ range to which the LISA band is sensitive. Modulations are negligible for $m_\chi \lesssim 10$~keV, reach the percent level by 40~keV, and then saturate to a CDM-like plateau, so the observable reliably probes $m_\chi$ only over the intermediate range $\sim 20$ to 40~keV. Repeating the 40~keV ensemble on identical subhalo catalogs with the cusp amplitude set to zero, we find that prompt cusps enhance the amplitude modulation only mildly. Where cusps make up a large fraction of the subhalo mass, free-streaming has already depleted the signal-carrying mass range, and where that range is populated, the cusp lies well inside the Fresnel radius, to which the diffraction integral responds through projected enclosed mass rather than central density. A percent-level detection in a strongly lensed massive black-hole binary would therefore establish the presence of substructure on Fresnel scales without diagnosing its inner profile.

repl.title: A Self-Consistent Jeans Analysis of the Milky Way Rotation Curve
repl.summary: Jeans-based measurements of the Milky Way (MW) rotation curve (RC) have revealed a declining outer RC. The interpretation, however, depends sensitively on the tracer selection, the tracer density profile, gradient terms in the Jeans equation, and non-axisymmetric perturbations in the outer disk. We present a more self-consistent Jeans analysis of the MW RC and reassess whether the outer decline remains after a revised treatment of the main Jeans terms and their associated systematic uncertainties, including those related to non-axisymmetric perturbations. We select a kinematically homogeneous disk tracer sample designed to retain stars on nearly circular disk orbits, removing only 12\% of the original sample. We estimate the tracer density profile from the same stars used for the kinematic moments, rather than adopting an external scale length. We find that the tracer density profile is better described by a double exponential over the validated range 12.5 < R < 21 kpc. We also assess the main systematic uncertainties associated with the fiducial Jeans equation terms, including the often neglected cross term, and account for different rotational velocities in the outer disk substructures. The derived RC remains nearly flat in the inner disk and declines at large radii. Over the adopted outer interval, $R\gtrsim16\,\mathrm{kpc}$, the RC slope is consistent with a Keplerian decline even after accounting for the systematic uncertainties. The corresponding mass modeling gives an extrapolated dynamical mass of $2.01^{+0.10}_{-0.08}\times10^{11}\,M_\odot$.

repl.title: Very High-Energy GRB Afterglow Fits with Neural-Network Emulation and Bayesian inference
repl.summary: The very high-energy ($E > 100$ GeV) afterglow emission in gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) can be explained by synchrotron self-Compton (SSC). Modeling this emission accurately requires fully numerical codes that solve the time-dependent coupled particle--photon kinetic equations while accounting for Klein--Nishina suppression. However, their substantial computational cost makes them impractical for traditional parameter inference techniques such as Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. In this work, we present a highly efficient surrogate model based on artificial neural networks (ANNs) that emulates a one-zone kinetic SSC radiation code. To train our ANN, we use a multi-dimensional model parameter grid that constitutes a sample of 100,800 spectra produced by an infinitely thin spherical blast wave propagating inside a constant density interstellar medium (ISM). The ANN reproduces the numerical spectra well, with the median relative error generally below 2 per cent across the full frequency domain. Using this surrogate framework, we perform Bayesian parameter posterior estimation via MCMC and fit the broadband GRB afterglow observations of GRB 190114C from X-rays to TeV $\gamma$-rays at different epochs. We find an energetic jet with isotropic-equivalent kinetic energy of $E_{\rm k,iso}\simeq7.2\times10^{54}$ erg moving with a coasting bulk Lorentz factor of $\Gamma\gtrsim500$ into an ISM with density $n\simeq0.1\,{\rm cm^{-3}}$. The deviation of our model light curve from observations on long timescales suggests that an ISM environment is inconsistent, and instead favours a radially stratified external medium.

repl.title: FAIR-Compliant Architecture for Heterogeneous Astronomical Data: KazVO Framework
repl.summary: This paper presents the architecture of the Kazakhstani National Virtual Observatory (KazVO) - an International Virtual Observatory Alliance (IVOA) compliant node that unifies the heterogeneous observational datasets of the Fesenkov Astrophysical Institute (FAI). The architectural foundation of the system is built upon a partitioned Data Lake, a German Astrophysical Virtual Observatory (GAVO) Data Center Helper Suite (DaCHS) publishing backend, and {a PostgreSQL database in which metadata for published observational products are mapped to IVOA ObsCore, while catalogs and simulation grids use dedicated relational tables}. We follow Open Science principles by introducing a metadata-only showcase model based on a four-class data embargo mechanism. Machine-to-Machine services deployed via IVOA protocols are exposed through the KazVO publishing registry registered in the global Registry of Registries (RofR), enabling analysis of Kazakhstani observational assets within external clients such as Tool for OPerations on Catalogues And Tables (TOPCAT), Aladin, and PyVO. The current implementation combines operational VO publication services and targeted photometric processing with scheduled, batch-mode data ingestion, supporting access to published historical and modern observational holdings. Replication has been validated on pilot datasets, while routine deployment at the observing sites and automated reduction of modern spectroscopic streams remain under development. The architecture provides a framework for progressively integrating these components into a complete data lifecycle.

repl.title: $r$-Process as Production of Lanthanides from Compact Object Mergers
repl.summary: The relative contributions of binary neutron star (BNS) and black hole-neutron star (BH-NS) mergers to the Galactic enrichment from the rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) remain an open question in nuclear astrophysics. In this paper, we present end-to-end numerical simulations of binary population synthesis, nucleosynthesis, and Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) via Compact Object Mergers: Population Astrophysics and Statistics (COMPAS), SkyNet network, and a stochastic multizone model, respectively. By considering five equations of state (EOSs) of NS and different spins of BH for BNS and BH-NS mergers, it is found that the averaged abundance seems not to be significantly dependent on the EOS of the neutron star (NS) and the spin of the BH for the BNS and BH-NS mergers. For the given EOSs of NS, the abundance of BNS is higher than that of BH-NS mergers before the second peak (for mass number $A\sim$130), but it is lower when the mass number is greater than 130. Moreover, the lighter $r$-process elements ($A<$130) are predominantly produced by the disk wind, while the heavier elements ($A>$130) originate mainly from the dynamical ejecta. The purely BNS mergers, on the other hand, are the dominant contributors to the production of lanthanides like europium (Eu) at the later stage of GCE, but BH-NS mergers make only a small contribution of heavy $r$-process elements for the $\rm Eu/Fe$ evolutionary tracks in the Milky Way.

repl.title: A comparison of particle and fluid approaches for modeling the streaming instability in global patch simulations
repl.summary: Identifying the process relevant to planet formation is still a major task. Mechanisms have been identified that can trap dust, preventing it from migrating inwards. A particular hydrodynamic instability, known as the streaming instability, is of high interest because it may be responsible for the formation of dust clumps from which the first planetesimals form. We aim to compare the outcome of non-linear streaming instability simulations using both fundamental approaches in a more realistic global disk model. The results will not be used to identify or disentangle the effect of, e.g., numerical diffusion in fluid simulations or the possibility of having crossing particle streams. Instead, they will enable us to determine whether the Lagrangian particle approach is the most suitable for numerical studies of the streaming instability. Methods: We perform 2D, axisymmetric, global, and isothermal hydrodynamic simulations using the two codes FARGO3D (dust fluid) and PLUTO (fluid, particles) to investigate the temporal evolution of dust scale height, midplane dust-to-gas ratio, and maximum dust density as well as to study velocity distributions and vorticities. For PLUTO particle simulations, we also investigate the influence of the gas Riemann solver and spatial reconstruction orders. Our results from a resolution study up to 5120 cells per gas scale height indicate convergence between PLUTO fluid and FARGO3D. Both yield a Gaussian profile dominated by small-scale, dust-depleted voids. Particle simulations with PLUTO have not yet converged, as a transient midplane dust component persists, indicating the need for even higher resolution or more particles. Using a more accurate Riemann solver or a higher-order spatial reconstruction scheme helps to bring the dust density profile closer to the converged structure.

repl.title: Wind-Fed Magnetic Flux and the Emergence of X-ray Coronae in Active Galactic Nuclei
repl.summary: We propose a scenario for the onset of radiatively efficient Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) in which circumnuclear stellar and supernova-driven winds supply mass and partially ordered magnetic flux to a compact disk reservoir around a supermassive black hole. A coherent poloidal component surviving advection to small radii strengthens inward, lowering the gas plasma beta until mean Maxwell stresses overtake MRI turbulence, compress the disk vertically, and open a magnetically dominated wedge above it. Within a quasi-force-free description of this wedge, the field self-organizes toward a critical twist at which the net radial transport changes sign, defining a magnetic saturation radius $r_c\sim10\,r_g$. The magnetic squeezing of the disk fixes the pressure balance at the interface between the disk and wedge, confining the accumulated flux at $r_c$: flux advected toward this boundary is preferentially shed, fixing $B_r\propto r^{-2}$ in the interior. From the field topology alone we then derive a normalized saturation flux $\phi \sim 50$, consistent with the MAD plateau of GRMHD simulations. The resulting compact, time-dependent saturation region is a natural candidate for the AGN X-ray corona, being collisionless, magnetized, and, at high compactness, plausibly pair-rich, with hadronic pair injection providing a conditional additional channel. Its size, variability, and spectral hardness are controlled by $r_c$, the compactness, and the magnetization. We connect these scalings to observed coronal sizes, variability, and the power partition between the corona and jet. We further propose that Little Red and Blue Dots could represent a disk-reservoir phase preceding luminous AGN activity.

repl.title: Discovery of the Slowest Radio Pulsar in the Small Magellanic Cloud
repl.summary: We report the discovery of a new radio pulsar PSR J0103$-$72 in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) through a reanalysis of Parkes/Murriyang archival observations targeting supernova remnants and pulsar-wind nebulae in the SMC. Previously two pulsars were discovered in these observations, and PSR J0103$-$72 is the third which we independently detected in two observations of its target field. It has a spin period of 1.327 sec and a dispersion measure (DM) of $272\pm13~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, making it the slowest known radio pulsar in the SMC with the second-highest DM. We did not identify any plausible supernova remnant or pulsar-wind nebula associated with the pulsar. Subtracting the predicted Galactic foreground leaves a DM contribution of $\sim 230$--$242~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, which may suggest a long path through the ionized medium of the SMC, enhanced ionized gas along the sightline, or both. Although these data had previously been searched using both FFT and fast folding algorithms, our FFT-based reprocessing found PSR J0103$-$72 through search techniques which have previously been highly effective in discovering a large number of pulsars in other surveys. This discovery shows that candidates with weak Fourier-domain significance can reveal faint, narrow-duty cycle pulsars missed in earlier extragalactic pulsar searches.

repl.title: Mergers may not be the main channel for galaxy stellar mass growth at redshift $z\gtrsim5$: Predictions from cosmological hierarchical models and simulations
repl.summary: Mergers are a crucial channel of galaxy growth, but their role relative to star formation remains uncertain at high redshift. Here we investigate merger rates and merger-driven stellar mass assembly for galaxies with stellar mass $M_\star \gtrsim 10^8 \, {\rm M_{\odot}}$ at $z\simeq 5-11$, by combining complementary theoretical approaches within $\Lambda$CDM. These include the DECODE semi-empirical model, the TNG100 and EAGLE hydrodynamical simulations, and the \textsc{L-Galaxies} semi-analytical model, together with the Millennium and TNG100-Dark simulations used to examine dark matter subhalo statistics and merger timescales. This compares models with different treatments of baryonic physics and galaxy-halo connections. We find that dark matter-only simulations predict merger timescales $\sim 30\%$ longer than those inferred from cosmological simulations including baryons. Galaxy major merger ($M_{\rm \star,sat} / M_{\rm \star,cen} > 0.25$) rates show a substantial model- and mass-dependent redshift evolution. Despite high rates, mergers contribute only $\lesssim 10\%$ to the total cosmic stellar mass density evolution. The average ex-situ stellar mass fraction ranges from a few percent to $\sim 25\%$ for all stellar mass bins at $z\gtrsim 5$, across different models and simulations. Their broad agreement implies that stellar mass assembly at cosmic dawn is dominated by in-situ star formation rather than mergers. These findings suggest that the high pair fractions identified by JWST may not directly trace efficient ex-situ stellar mass growth, highlighting the need for physically motivated merger timescales to interpret galaxy assembly in the early Universe.

repl.title: A Parsec-scale Circumstellar Shell Around VX Sgr: Mass Loss and RSG/TŻO Nature
repl.summary: A thin, arc-shaped shell is discovered surrounding VX Sagittarii (VX Sgr), the largest known CSM shell around an RSG at a scale $r\sim0.59\,\mathrm{pc}$. The nebula has an extinction-corrected H$\alpha$ intensity $I_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}\sim38\,\mathrm{R}$ and an ionized mass $\sim0.1\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. The slow $12\,\mathrm{km\,s}^{-1}$ peculiar velocity of VX Sgr and the lack of far-infrared emission in the arc indicate that it is not produced by a bow shock, but is likely instead steady RSG wind or ejecta that is photoionized by a nearby $\mathrm{O}$- or $\mathrm{B}$- type star. The nature of VX Sgr is debated in the literature as a red supergiant/hypergiant (RSG/RHG), super-AGB star, or Thorne--Żytkow Object (TŻO). Using the kinematic age of the Sgr OB1 association, the super-AGB model is disfavored. A spectroscopic test of the arc is proposed to potentially distinguish an RSG from a possible TŻO. The mass-loss rate is estimated from the geometry and emission measure of the shell, finding $\dot{M}\approx4\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. The future interaction of the supernova (SN) ejecta of VX Sgr and the surrounding circumstellar material (CSM) is briefly explored through the mass ratio $\Lambda$ of the shell and SN ejecta; the interaction would likely not have a significant effect on the SN forward shock.

repl.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). XLV. Data processing for intracluster light measurements
repl.summary: The Euclid survey provides images with extraordinary potential for studies of the low-surface-brightness Universe, including intracluster light (ICL). However, to realise this promise, the data must be carefully treated to minimise background variations while preserving the signal from diffuse structures. In this work, we describe the post-processing and measurement procedures used for studies of ICL with Euclid. We demonstrate a substantial reduction in background variations without resorting to a small-scale background subtraction. By injecting simulated clusters into the real images, we show that our approach preserves the faint outskirts of extended sources. On scales of several arcminutes, we can reliably detect surface-brightness levels around 27.5 mag arcsec$^{-2}$ in $Y_\textrm{E}$, $J_\textrm{E}$, $H_\textrm{E}$, and 29 mag arcsec$^{-2}$ in $I_\textrm{E}$. As a result, we can obtain accurate measurements of the ICL in individual clusters from the local Universe out to z~0.8 with uncertainties of the order of 10% in surface brightness, 10 degrees in position angle, and 0.1 in ellipticity. Our ability to measure the diffuse light with Euclid is thus set to meet expectations and revolutionise our understanding of the ICL.

repl.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). XLVII. The shape of cluster haloes revealed by intracluster light
repl.summary: Intracluster light (ICL) offers a luminous route for measuring the shapes and orientations of cluster haloes. We used Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1) images to quantify ICL shapes for 205 clusters at $0.1 \leq z \leq 0.8$ selected from the eROSITA All-Sky Survey and the Dark Energy Survey. We measured the ICL properties across five bands ($I_\mathrm{E}$, $Y_\mathrm{E}$, $J_\mathrm{E}$, $H_\mathrm{E}$ and the coadded $YJH_\mathrm{E}$), and find that the shape parameters are consistent across the filters, with the $H_\mathrm{E}$ band probing the profiles to the largest cluster-centric distances ($0.1R_{200\mathrm{c}}\sim100$ kpc). The ICL ellipticity ($e=1-b/a$) distribution peaks at 0.5, consistent with halo ellipticities inferred from strong and weak lensing studies, suggesting that the ICL traces the large-scale structure of the clusters. Cluster cores, dominated by brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) light, are round ($e\sim0.2$), while the ICL becomes progressively more elongated at large radii, reaching an ellipticity of $\sim0.5$ by $0.1R_{200\mathrm{c}}$. We find that the ICL is closely aligned with the BCG (87% lie within 30$^\circ$), but shows a weaker alignment with the satellite galaxy distribution (61% within 30$^\circ$). Robust position angles could be measured using the ICL for 63% of the sample, whereas position angles could be measured for only 30% of the sample using the satellite galaxies. Stacking clusters in redshift bins allows measurements of the ICL surface brightness to $0.6$-$0.8R_{200\mathrm{c}}$ and ellipticity beyond $0.3$-$0.4R_{200\mathrm{c}}$ (300-400 kpc), but we observed a plateau in the ICL ellipticity beyond $0.1R_{200\mathrm{c}}$. These results demonstrate the capability of Euclid to characterise the ICL morphology with high statistical precision, allowing new constraints on cluster halo structure and its evolution with redshift.

repl.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). XLVIII. A systematic study of the intracluster light fraction at 0.2 < z < 1.5
repl.summary: We present a homogeneous analysis of the intracluster light (ICL) in approximately 300 galaxy clusters spanning $0.2<z<1.5$, combining Sunyaev-Zeldovich-selected clusters from the South Pole Telescope and optically selected clusters from Euclid, and comparing results with Hydrangea simulations. We measured the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) within elliptical isophotes of semi-major axis 50 kpc, and ICL between 50 and 200 kpc. We show that the Euclid Wide Survey can detect ICL in individual massive clusters ($M_{500} \gtrsim 10^{14.2}\,M_{\odot}$) out to at least $z\sim1.5$, with detection rates of 70-80%. This indicates that diffuse stellar envelopes are common, although not ubiquitous, in massive clusters throughout this redshift range. Using a uniform methodology, we place improved constraints on ICL fraction evolution. ICL contributes about 40% of the combined BCG and ICL light and 20% of the total cluster stellar light, with both fractions remaining approximately constant across $0.2<z<1.5$ at fixed cluster mass. This implies that the relative partitioning of stellar mass between the BCG, ICL, and satellite populations is largely established by $z\sim1.5$. However, the ICL properties of individual clusters may still change as they evolve, since the sample does not represent an evolutionary sequence. This behaviour is consistent with a scenario in which the BCG and ICL are assembled together through the accretion, stripping, and eventual merging of the same population of massive galaxies ($>10^{10}\,M_\odot$). The inferred ICL fraction also depends systematically on wavelength, while remaining largely insensitive to the adopted outer integration radius of 200-600 kpc. These results highlight the importance of homogeneous ICL analyses and constrain the evolution of diffuse stellar components in clusters.

repl.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). XLVI. The metallicity of the intracluster light
repl.summary: Colour provides key information to constrain the stellar population of the intracluster light (ICL), the diffuse light within galaxy clusters. We derive radial colour profiles ($Y_\mathrm{E}-H_\mathrm{E}$, $J_\mathrm{E}-H_\mathrm{E}$, $I_\mathrm{E}-H_\mathrm{E}$) of the brightest central galaxy (BCG) and ICL for 168 galaxy clusters from the Dark Energy Survey redMaPPer catalogue within the redshift range $0.1 < z < 0.75$ and halo mass $M_{\rm 200m} > 10^{14.05}M_\odot/h$, within the Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). By stacking the light profiles measured using elliptical annuli on the BCG and ICL images, we reliably measure the ICL colour out to approximately 300 kpc, over which we find a colour gradient, with the ICL becoming bluer than the BCG out to approximately 150 kpc. Using stellar population synthesis (SPS) models, we find that near-infrared (NIR) colours are sensitive to metallicity, but not age. Thus, we measure a metallicity profile in the BCG and ICL that extends out to 300 kpc for a statistical sample for the first time. While the colours, and the detection of a colour and metallicity gradient, are robust, we note that our metallicity measurement is dependent upon our choice of both SPS model and colour. We find that the metallicity of the BCG is super-solar [$\log_{10} (Z/Z_\odot) > 0.1$], while the ICL is metal-poor [$\log_{10}(Z/Z_\odot)\approx -0.5$], placing the first statistical constraint on the metallicity of the ICL out to large radii. These results support our current understanding of BCG and ICL formation: BCGs form predominantly through mergers with massive galaxies or the cores of satellite galaxies, while the ICL grows via the tidal stripping of lower-metallicity stars from the outskirts of massive satellite galaxies.

repl.title: Model of the instrumental polarization induced by a rotating HWP with anti-reflective sub-wavelength structures for CMB polarimetry
repl.summary: Future CMB polarization experiments require precise control of instrumental systematics in the search for primordial $B$-mode polarization. A rotating half-wave plate (HWP) provides effective polarization modulation, but its non-ideal electromagnetic response can generate HWP-synchronous instrumental polarization. In this work, we characterize the response of a multi-layer sapphire HWP with anti-reflective sub-wavelength structures (SWS) using rigorous coupled-wave analysis. For three asymmetric SWS models, we find no substantial differences in the transmittance, polarization efficiency, or instrumental-polarization response that can be attributed to the type of SWS asymmetry. The fourth-harmonic instrumental polarization relevant to CMB polarization reconstruction is typically of order $10^{-4}$ in the CMB bands, which is expected to be mitigated. We further evaluate an actually fabricated SWS geometry, whose asymmetry enhances the retardance, and compare its response with that of an idealized model having the same type of asymmetry. Comparison of the realistic SWS with the idealized model shows that higher transmittance tends to be associated with lower instrumental polarization. These results suggest that improving the total transmission, including the effect of the fabricated SWS profile, may be more important for reducing HWP-induced instrumental polarization than tuning the SWS asymmetry itself.

repl.title: Can the $\sim 5$ kpc starburst ring in the Milky Way create the eROSITA bubbles?
repl.summary: eROSITA bubbles (eRBs) in our Galaxy are thought to be due to the energy injection by the central star-forming region or the central supermassive black hole. Identifying the origin of these bubbles is crucial in constraining the origin of the Fermi Bubbles and the nature of the Galactic feedback. However, some recent opinions suggest that the eRBs may not even have been produced by any central source, but rather a result of a star-formation ring at $R\sim 5$ kpc. In this letter, we perform detailed hydrodynamic simulations to refute that claim and show that such a ring of star formation alone is not able to produce the symmetric eROSITA bubbles - one needs a compact energy injection from the Galactic Center to produce these bubbles. Our study, therefore, suggests that the eROSITA bubbles truly represent the nuclear outflow from our Galaxy.

repl.title: HD 210058 b and BD+37 4838 b: A precessing eccentric hot Jupiter and a misaligned substellar companion around two A-type stars
repl.summary: Relatively few A- and F-type stars are known to host exoplanets, and likewise few planets have measured spin-orbit angles, defined as the angle between the planet's orbital axis and the star's rotational axis. Expanding the sample of such systems is important for constraining the formation and migration mechanisms of close-in giant planets around early-type stars. We aim to measure the sky-projected spin-orbit angles of HD 210058b (TOI-1355b) and BD+37 4838b (TOI-1414b), two objects listed as candidate exoplanets, and assess the planetary nature of these systems. Both of their host stars are fast rotators. We analyzed TESS photometry in combination with the transit time series of HARPS-N spectra. For both objects, we created cross-correlation functions from the spectra to analyze Doppler tomography and detect and model the Doppler shadow. We also used photometric observations to refine several poorly constrained photometric and spectroscopic parameters of both the host stars and their companions. When possible, we used the derived results to constrain the companion masses. We verified the planetary and substellar nature for both objects. We report HD 210058b to be a giant hot Jupiter with a mass of $\sim10\,\mathrm{M_{Jup}}$, residing on a slightly misaligned orbit with a sky-projected spin-orbit angle $\lambda=-32_{-6}^{+4}$ deg. Archival photometry reveals a continuously changing inclination and impact parameter, indicating nodal precession with a period of $\sim860$ yr and implying that further transit observations will be possible for only about six more years. The second target, BD+37 4838b, orbits a hybrid $\gamma$ Dor-$\delta$ Sct pulsator on a misaligned orbit with $\lambda=56.9^{+1.4}_{-2.3}$ deg. Since we could not reliably recover its mass, we only report an upper limit of $\sim24.3\,\mathrm{M_{Jup}}$, leaving the possible planetary nature of this object unresolved.

repl.title: Recovering Missing Degrees of Freedom in Simulation-Trained Field-Level Generative Models
repl.summary: Simulation-trained generative models are emerging as a powerful framework for field-level inference in cosmology, particularly in strongly nonlinear regimes where analytical approaches become intractable. However, the finite size of training datasets often leads to variance shrinkage, indicating that part of the realization-level variability of the underlying physical process is not captured by the learned generative dynamics. In this paper, we interpret variance shrinkage as a diagnostic of missing effective degrees of freedom and introduce physics-informed latent modifications to the generative dynamics of a continuous normalizing flow. We show that these latent corrections recover a substantial fraction of the missing variability without requiring additional training simulations. Using weak-lensing field-level inference as a representative cosmological application, we further demonstrate through posterior analysis that the learned latent directions are actively exploited during inference and behave as effective nuisance parameters that absorb part of the mismatch between the training and target distributions. As a result, the model exhibits improved robustness to out-of-distribution shifts in field-level inference. Our work establishes variance shrinkage as a practical diagnostic for identifying missing degrees of freedom in simulation-trained generative models and provides a framework for recovering them through physics-informed modifications of generative dynamics.

repl.title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
repl.summary: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.

repl.title: Breaking dark degeneracies in $k$-essence models with redshift-space distortions
repl.summary: Dynamical dark energy models are often difficult to constrain with background observations alone due to parameter degeneracies. This is especially true when the dark energy sector evolves through an effective pressureless matter phase, leading to degeneracies between the model parameters and the matter density parameter. In this work, we show that redshift-space distortion (RSD) measurements help break this degeneracy when combined with expansion history probes including Pantheon$^{+}$ supernovae and DESI DR2 BAO measurements. We demonstrate this in the ghost and dilatonic ghost condensate $k$-essence models, restricting the observational analysis to physically admissible solutions by imposing the absence of ghosts and gradient instabilities. Given the small scalar sound speeds in these models, we also explicitly check the validity of the quasi-static approximation used in the growth analysis. Our results show that combining growth-rate data with stability requirements and standard background observations provides a fast and efficient way to constrain potentially degenerate dark sector models.

repl.title: FORGE'd in the Early Universe II: Constraining the Pop III Initial Mass Function
repl.summary: We present a cosmological radiation-magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) zoom-in simulation of $56$ Population III stars using FORGE'd in FIRE. Our simulation combines a cosmological initial condition centered on an isolated ultra-faint galaxy ($M_{\mathrm{halo}} \sim 10^9 M_\odot$ at $z=0$) with individual-star formation and feedback physics, reaching a maximum mass resolution of $\sim 10^{-2} M_\odot$ and spatial resolution of $\sim 10^{-3} \mathrm{pc}$. We follow continued star formation for just over $500$ Myr, from $z \sim 16$ to $z \sim 7$, substantially longer than what has been achieved before, and track star formation across five distinct minihalos. From our stellar population, we self-consistently resolve an emergent stellar initial mass function (IMF) and find $\alpha = 1.9$ for $dN/dM \propto M^{-\alpha}$ at $M_{\star} \gtrsim 2.2 M_{\odot}$. Additionally, we form both single and multiple stellar systems, including binaries and higher-order multiples, as well as stars with masses below $1 M_{\odot}$. At early times, the stellar mass distribution is more top-heavy, with a high-mass slope of $\alpha\sim1.4-1.5$, similar to previous Pop. III simulations, and steepens as star formation continues. This suggests that differences between our final IMF and previous studies may partly reflect the much longer evolution followed here, approximately five orders of magnitude longer than in several previous Pop. III sink-particle simulations. The first star-forming minihalo, which hosts the most massive stars in our simulation, has a shallower IMF slope of $\alpha\approx 1$, while later-forming minihalos produce lower maximum stellar masses in lower-density parent clouds.

Darker colors are regions of lower density, while brighter colors indicate higher density. repl.title: Enhanced Mid-Photospheric Heating Around a Solar Pore
repl.summary: We present depth-stratified atmospheric reconstructions of a solar pore observed with the Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared SpectroPolarimeter (SCIP) aboard \textsc{Sunrise~iii}. Using spatially coupled NLTE spectropolarimetric inversions, we characterize the thermal, magnetic, and velocity structure of the pore and its surroundings from the photosphere to the chromosphere over approximately two hours. The inversions recover the canonical photospheric properties of pores: a cool umbra with strong magnetic fields dominated by the vertical component. Most photospheric velocities are subsonic, but localized downflows near the pore boundary reach transonic or potentially supersonic values around $\log\tau_{500}=0$. At higher atmospheric layers, the thermal contrast between the pore and its surroundings decreases substantially. We also detect localized mid-photospheric temperature enhancements forming a patchy, ring-like structure in the wings of the Ca\,{\sc ii} 8542\,Å line, without a clear continuum counterpart. The temperature excess reaches approximately $300$\,K and corresponds to an excess thermal-energy density of up to $170$\,J\,m$^{-3}$. These regions coincide with an enhanced transverse magnetic-field component and the expanding magnetic canopy surrounding the pore. The structure is detected in all three rasters, although the cadence does not establish whether individual patches persist or repeatedly re-form. While the heating mechanism cannot be uniquely identified, the inferred magnetic topology supports an association with processes operating in the expanding canopy. These results demonstrate the value of pores for investigating the coupling between magnetic topology, convection, and atmospheric energy transport.

repl.title: Simulation of a Jovian Planet Undergoing Gas Accretion
repl.summary: To understand the process of planet formation in the Solar System or any other stellar system, we need to comprehend the interaction between forming planets and the protoplanetary disk. This work presents a study of the interaction of the protoplanetary disk with the protoplanet and the following types of orbital migration that can occur, and to verify this interaction, numerical simulations were performed using the magneto-hydrodynamics code FARGO3D. The researchers made five simulations with a 2-Jupiter-mass planet in the protoplanetary disk. The only parameter varied was the initial radial position with the aim of verifying the influence of this parameter on the behavior of planetary migration. As a result of these simulations, we find that the initial radial coordinate is a very significant parameter in how the planet interacts with the gas in the disk and the formation of gas gaps.

repl.title: Millimeter-Wavelength Constraints on Circular Polarization of the Cosmic Microwave Background at Arcminute Scales with the Simons Array
repl.summary: We present constraints on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) circular polarization anisotropy at arcminute angular scales, using dedicated measurements from the Simons Array taken with a quarter-wave plate and rotating half-wave plate. A detection of circular polarization in the CMB would probe a range of proposed generation mechanisms, from Standard Model astrophysics to physics beyond it. At an observing frequency of 90 GHz, we place constraints over the multipole range $300 \leq \ell \leq 2000$, corresponding to angular scales of 5.4-36 arcmin, in bands of width $\Delta \ell = 100$, roughly tripling the highest multipole previously reached by a $V$-mode power spectrum measurement. Within this domain, we constrain the 95% confidence upper bound of $\ell (\ell+1) C_\ell^{VV} / (2\pi)$ to range from $\sim 22\,\mu\mathrm{K}_\mathrm{CMB}^2$ at the $\ell = 350$ bandpower to $\sim 3.5 \times 10^3\,\mu\mathrm{K}_\mathrm{CMB}^2$ at the $\ell = 1950$ bandpower. These limits are derived from $\sim$2.5 months of observations of each of two small regions of the sky located away from the Galactic plane, totaling $\sim$12 deg$^2$ of effective sky area. Because the methodology of this study marginalizes known foreground contamination, these bounds serve as robust, conservative limits on the true CMB circular polarization signal down to the sensitivity limits of the instrument. Additionally, we provide an experimental and analytical framework for implementing circular polarization observations on other telescopes by utilizing a quarter-wave plate and half-wave plate design.

repl.title: Early--Narrow and Late--Wide Populations of GRB X-ray Flares
repl.summary: The physical origin of gamma-ray burst (GRB) X-ray flares remains debated, particularly whether they arise from prolonged central-engine activity or from variability in the external shock. Building on our previous analysis of 89 Swift GRBs with measured redshifts, we investigate the rest-frame temporal properties of X-ray flares detected in 61 bursts. We apply a multivariate Gaussian Mixture Model to rest-frame peak times and widths. We identify two statistically distinct populations: early-narrow flares (80%), with characteristic peak times of approximately 10^2 s and w/t_pk <= 1, and late-wide flares (20%), with characteristic peak times of ~ 10^3.5 s and w/t_pk >= 2. Of the 61 single or first flares, 55 belong to the early-narrow population and only 6 to the late-wide population. Of the 36 second flares, 23 (64%) belong to the early-narrow population, with shorter waiting times, whereas 13 (36%) belong to the late-wide population, with substantially longer waiting times. The width-peak-time correlation remains significant for early-narrow flares but not for late-wide flares. Furthermore, we find no correlation between flare width and energy. We find a decline of flare luminosity with peak time, driven primarily by the early-narrow population, but not statistically significant for late-wide flares. These results imply that a simple shift in time, potentially associated with later episodes of central-engine activity, cannot explain the distinction between the two flare populations. On the other hand, the peak times are consistent with expectations from an accretion disk formed following the collapse of a stellar-size massive star. Combined with our previous finding that flare properties are independent of the presence of an X-ray plateau, these results favor prolonged accretion-driven central-engine activity over external-shock variability as the primary origin of X-ray flares.

repl.title: Flux Variation of the Crab Pulsar Observed Using Fermi LAT and NuSTAR
repl.summary: The flux of pulsed emission from the Crab pulsar, just like most of other pulsars, is considered to be steady over time scales much larger than the pulsation period, except for a smooth, secular decrease related to the aging of pulsars. Such a steady assumption prevails in all theoretical investigations of pulsar emission models. However, here we report the discovery of stochastic variation in the flux and photon index of the Crab pulsar gamma-ray and hard X-ray emissions utilizing archival data of Fermi LAT (0.1 -- 100 GeV, spanning 17 years) and of NuSTAR (3.0 -- 79.0 keV, spanning 13 years) observations. Furthermore, the flux variation is found to be anti-correlated with variation of the spectral photon index, that is, harder when brighter, in both gamma ray and hard X-ray bands. The origin of such variation is intriguing. Some possibilities are discussed.

repl.title: Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory
repl.summary: Studies of the arrival-direction distribution of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays are crucial for revealing their origin. In this work, we investigate the distribution of the arrival directions of events detected with the Pierre Auger Observatory over different angular scales. To do this, we adopt a novel method where we use a von Mises--Fisher distribution to model the excesses with respect to isotropic expectations. This method allows us to study the distribution of arrival directions over different angular scales consistently and simultaneously. We consider the events in different energy bins above 4 EeV detected from 1$^\text{st}$ January 2004 to 31$^\text{st}$ December 2022, i.e. during the entire Phase~I of the Pierre Auger Observatory, with a total exposure of $123{,}000$ km$^2$ sr yr. The most significant excess in the bins considered is a dipolar modulation in the energy range (8--16) EeV, which is compatible with previous findings of the Pierre Auger Collaboration. A dipolar modulation appears to be present for the higher energies considered as well, and at the highest energies, i.e. above 32 EeV, we find indications of its coexistence with an overdensity of intermediate angular scale, located in the Centaurus region.

repl.title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
repl.summary: Ultrahigh energy neutrinos ($E_\nu \gtrsim 100$ PeV) are detectable through Askaryan emission---the nanosecond-scale radio impulse emitted by relativistic particle cascades in a dielectric medium. The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA), an Askaryan detector array located at the South Pole, has been taking data for more than a decade. We present the first array-wide search for diffuse ultrahigh energy neutrinos with ARA. The search found no events on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. The resulting upper limit is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV and provides the first constraints on the flux reported by the KM3NeT Collaboration that are complementary to optical Cherenkov and particle detectors. This limit also constrains UHECR source models, and excludes some models with trans-GZK proton populations at the $90\%$ confidence level. This represents the largest Askaryan detector dataset ever analyzed, demonstrating the feasibility and sensitivity of searches with large detector arrays acting as a single observatory. It also underscores the high acceptance and exposure of Askaryan detector arrays to ultrahigh energy neutrinos.

repl.title: Analysis Methodology of the Search for Ultrahigh Energy Neutrinos in 10.6 Years of Askaryan Radio Array Data
repl.summary: The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA) is an in-ice radio observatory at the South Pole designed to detect ultrahigh energy (UHE) neutrinos through Askaryan emission produced by interactions of neutrinos and their secondary particles. In this paper, we present the detailed methodology of the first array-wide search for a diffuse UHE neutrino flux using data from all five ARA stations. The dataset considered represents $10.6$ years of livetime and is three times larger than previous ARA neutrino searches. This search achieves a $28\%$ analysis efficiency for a neutrino flux corresponding to the current experimental upper limits. No neutrino candidates are observed on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. We set a new upper limit on the diffuse UHE neutrino flux, which is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV. We also discuss lessons learned for future searches on large radio arrays.

repl.title: r-Process Abundance Variations in Globular Clusters as Fossils of Turbulent Mixing
repl.summary: Several metal-poor Galactic globular clusters exhibit substantial star-to-star $r$-process abundance variations at nearly fixed [Fe/H], with the ensemble suggesting smaller variations toward increasing metallicity. We investigate whether this chemical structure can be inherited from incomplete mixing in the galactic environments in which the clusters formed. Using parsec-scale simulations of rare-element transport in a supernova-driven turbulent disk, we follow the redistribution of $r$-process ejecta and characterize the abundance structure of gas selected to trace star-forming environments. Rare enrichment events generate strong [Eu/Fe] inhomogeneities that persist across a range of physical scales. As chemical evolution proceeds, the available abundance variance decreases, while spatial averaging over larger regions reduces the differences between their characteristic abundances. The simulations provide substantial pre-collapse $r$-process variance at low [Fe/H] and show the same broad decline toward higher metallicity suggested by the globular-cluster measurements. Our results support an interpretation in which at least some of the observed $r$-process variations are inherited from pre-existing chemical structure in the natal environment, allowing globular clusters to preserve a fossil record of the mixing history between rare enrichment and star formation.

repl.title: Stellar evolution and axion-like particles: new constraints and hints from globular clusters in the GAIA DR3 data
repl.summary: Axion-like particles (ALPs) are hypothetical pseudoscalar bosons, natural in extensions of the Standard Model. Their interactions with ordinary matter and radiation are suppressed, making it challenging to detect them in laboratory experiments. However, these particles, produced within stellar interiors, can provide an additional mechanism for energy loss, potentially influencing stellar evolution. Prominent methods for searching for such effects involve measuring the properties of red giants and helium-burning stars in globular clusters (GCs). Here we use published catalogs of stars selected as members of seven GCs on the basis of parallaxes and proper motions measured by Gaia (Data Release 3). Making use of previously derived theoretical relations and the new data, we find the upper limit on the ALP-electron coupling, g_{ae}<1.3*10^{-13} (95% CL), and an indication (2.6 sigma) to nonzero ALP-photon coupling, g_{a\gamma}=(6.6+1.3-1.8)*10^{-11} GeV^{-1}. Given the precision of contemporary observational data, it is imperative to refine ALP constraints through more sophisticated analyses, which will be explored in detail elsewhere.

repl.title: Robust Amortized Simulation-Based Inference via Learned Error Models
repl.summary: Recent advances in neural density estimation have enabled amortized Bayesian inference for complex stochastic simulators. However, these methods rely on simulators accurately reflecting the true data-generating process and can degrade significantly under model misspecification. We consider the setting where multiple unlabeled observations are available and introduce robust variational neural posterior estimation (RVNP), an amortized Bayesian inference method that uses an importance-weighted autoencoder to jointly learn a misspecification-robust posterior proxy and an explicit error model that captures the simulation-to-reality gap. Our results show that RVNP can recover robust posterior inference in a data-driven and interpretable manner, outperforming previous methods on multiple metrics across misspecified benchmarks.

repl.title: Popcorn EMRIs: Transient Gravitational Wave Signals and Their Analysis in Schwartz Space
repl.summary: This study investigates extreme-mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) with orbital periods exceeding the observation windows of mHz gravitational wave detectors. During their early, highly eccentric stages, these systems produce periodic gravitational wave eruptions at pericentre, separated by long quiescent periods. We define these systems as ``popcorn EMRIs''--bound, coherent binaries in a deterministic evolutionary phase. This distinguishes them from stochastic, non-coherent bursts associated with parabolic fly-bys. Using a steady-state model based on the phase-space continuity equation, we estimate the population within a Milky Way-like galaxy. Because these estimates depend on sensitive astrophysical variables like stellar relaxation and density profiles, our figures are illustrative rather than absolute. For a one-year observation baseline, we estimate a steady-state population of 200 to 2,000 popcorn EMRIs, significantly outnumbering the 10 to 88 continuously observable EMRIs. This yields an expected rate of 5 to 44 detectable eruptions per year. Despite high signal-to-noise ratios (exceeding 700 for Galactic Centre events), the low duty cycle confirms their transient nature. Standard data processing techniques, designed for continuous signals, often employ windowing that distorts eruption morphology and artificially reduces the signal-to-noise ratio. To address this, we establish a mathematical apparatus using based on standard smoothing techniques, in the theory of tempered distributions. We demonstrate that standard windowing techniques irreversibly degrade the signal-to-noise ratio of transient sources when the taper overlaps the eruption, and we utilize Schwartz space regularization to justify the direct Fourier transform as the energy-preserving estimator.

repl.title: MarsRetrieval: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Planetary-Scale Geospatial Retrieval on Mars
repl.summary: Data-driven approaches like deep learning are rapidly advancing planetary science, particularly in Mars exploration. Despite recent progress, most existing benchmarks remain confined to closed-set supervised visual tasks and do not support text-guided retrieval for geospatial discovery. We introduce MarsRetrieval, a retrieval benchmark for evaluating vision-language models for Martian geospatial discovery. MarsRetrieval includes three tasks: (1) paired image-text retrieval, (2) landform retrieval, and (3) global geo-localization, covering multiple spatial scales and diverse geomorphic origins. We propose a unified retrieval-centric protocol to benchmark multimodal embedding architectures, including contrastive dual-tower encoders and generative vision-language models. Our evaluation shows MarsRetrieval is challenging: even strong foundation models often fail to capture domain-specific geomorphic distinctions. We further show that domain-specific fine-tuning is critical for generalizable geospatial discovery in planetary settings. Our code is available at this https URL

repl.title: Ion pickup and velocity space thermalization at outer planet moons
repl.summary: Ion pickup at the outer planets' active moons is a fundamental plasma process in which newly ionized particles from moon exospheres interact with the ambient corotating plasma and are accelerated to match the background flow. Spacecraft observations have revealed intense electromagnetic wave activity commonly attributed to this pickup process. Here we investigate ion pickup using hybrid-kinetic simulations in which ions are treated kinetically while electrons are modeled as a massless fluid. In the moon's rest frame, ambient ions initially stream perpendicular to the background magnetic field at the corotation velocity, creating a nongyrotropic velocity distribution with two ion populations clustered at opposite gyrophases. Within a few ion gyroperiods, this configuration simultaneously excites transverse magnetic perturbations associated with electromagnetic ion cyclotron waves and compressional perturbations associated with mirror-mode and ion Bernstein waves, reaching amplitudes of several percent of the background field strength. Using field-particle correlation analysis, we quantify the energy transfer between waves and particles and demonstrate how these perturbations scatter ions in velocity space, efficiently incorporating newly created ions into the background plasma and leading to isotropization in both gyrophase and pitch angle. These results provide a kinetic framework for understanding pickup-driven wave-particle interactions and offer guidance for interpreting in situ measurements at active moons throughout the outer solar system.
